first.rationale: Targeted pricing most directly addresses the immediate loss of price-sensitive SMB accounts and has prior acquisition and revenue evidence. Verify its segment design and downstream quality, while using onboarding evidence as the strongest alternative given the completion decline. Keep the test guarded because discount-driven gains may not translate into sustainable qualified revenue.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. The verified source showed higher completion, faster time-to-value, and improved 30-day retention, directly addressing the current onboarding decline while supporting sustainable revenue. Reject promotional pricing this cycle because its verified retention decline undermines long-term qualified revenue despite short-term gains.

final2.rationale: Proceed with shortened onboarding. Verified evidence shows improved completion, faster time-to-value, and higher 30-day retention, directly supporting sustainable qualified revenue. The competitor’s deeper cut increases urgency but does not reverse our verified finding that a 40% targeted discount produced materially worse retention. Promotional pricing is therefore rejected absent new evidence that a different offer structure can preserve cohort quality.
